howDoI.q: How do I make a block that gives my hero a power?
How do I make my hero jump higher?
How do I put the exit where only a power can reach?
How do I make a power that runs out?
How do I make my hero walk faster?
How do I make a gap that needs a power to cross?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Power Up is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels about powers, and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each power is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

pages.head: Level 1: The High Ledge
pages.html:
Level 1: The High Ledge

The exit door stands on a ledge of planks five blocks up. The THE EXIT IS UP ON THAT LEDGE sign stands under it. Jump, and the hero goes up about three blocks and comes back down: it is too high. Nothing is hurt, and you can try as often as you like.

Walk on to the right. A second sign and two stars wait on the grass. Touch a star and it is gone: the sign says it gives four high jumps. Go back under the ledge, jump, and steer right: the hero rises about six blocks and lands on the planks. The ordinary jump comes back by itself once the four are used. A second star is there if you waste some.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A block that gives a power. Open power.bbl in the blocks editor and pick star. Its Changes counter is the counter of sequence 9 and its by is 4. A block can add to a counter when touched, and the counters numbered 5 to 19 belong to the hero's sequences: counter 9 is the one of sequence 9, the jump on Space. The star is not solid and becomes plain sky when touched, so you take it once, the way you take a coin.
  • The high jump. Open hero.chr in the character editor and look at sequence 9. Its first frame pushes the hero up by 17 pixels instead of 12, so they rise about 121 pixels (six blocks) instead of 66 (three). Its counter starts at 0, and a sequence with a counter of 0 cannot start.
  • The ordinary jump. Sequence 17 is the old jump, with the same Space key and no limit. When you press a key, Game-Maker starts the first sequence with that key that still has uses left, counting from 0. The high jump comes first, so it wins while it has uses. At 0 uses the ordinary jump on sequence 17 takes over. That is the whole trick behind a power.
  • It runs out by use, not by time. Each time a sequence starts it counts down by one. Game-Maker has no clock that switches a power off, so a power that wears out is a power with a count. Press F2: the screen does not show sequence counters, so a sign can say how many there are, as this one does.
  • The ledge. Open one.map. The ledge is a row of plank blocks, the same ones the hero can stand on and jump up through. The exit door stands on it, and the hero's scene link is the door's bottom block. The ledge is five blocks above the ground: more than the ordinary jump, less than the high one.
  • Visible limits. Brick walls close both ends, so nothing stops the hero that you cannot see.

pages.head: Level 2: The Wide Gap
pages.html:
Level 2: The Wide Gap

You start in the middle of a long room. To the right a canyon cuts the ground, seven blocks wide. The TOO WIDE TO JUMP sign says to look back the way you came. Try the jump anyway: the hero drops to the canyon floor. It does not hurt. Two steps on the near wall bring you out: hop up them.

To the left, past a second sign, lie a pair of red sneakers, one for each foot. Walk over both. Now Left and Right move you twice as fast, and a jump goes twice as far. Run to the canyon and leap: the hero lands on the far side. The sneakers last fifty strides each way, and then the ordinary walk comes back.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Faster walking. Open hero.chr and look at sequences 5 and 6: walking right and left. Each frame moves the hero 8 pixels instead of 4, and their counters start at 0. The ordinary walks are sequences 18 and 19, with the same keys and no limit. The same rule as level 1: the first sequence on a key with uses left runs, so the sneakers win until their count is gone.
  • Why a pair? A block can add to only one counter, and left and right are two sequences. So there are two blocks: sneakerR adds 50 to counter 5 and sneakerL adds 50 to counter 6. A copy of the game that only wants a faster run to the right needs only the first. A stride is one trip through a sequence's four frames, about a fifth of a second.
  • A longer jump comes free. In the air the hero moves sideways by the walking sequence for the key held. Faster walking means a longer leap. An ordinary jump carries them a little over four blocks and the sneakers' leap a little under nine. The canyon is seven wide, so one falls short and the other lands.
  • The canyon. In two.map it is seven blocks wide and four deep, cut out of the grass and dirt, with a floor under it. A fall into it hurts nothing, and an ordinary jump (three blocks) cannot climb out, so two steps of dirt stand against its near wall, one block and two blocks high. Each is a block the hero can stand on, within one jump of the one before. Nothing here has to be climbed with Up.
  • Not time. As in level 1, nothing times a power out. The sneakers last for strides, so a hero who stands still keeps them forever.
  • Visible limits. Brick walls close both ends of the room, and the canyon you can see is the only place you can fall.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Make a star give 10 high jumps: change its by in power.bbl.
  • Make the high jump higher: change the first frame of sequence 9 in hero.chr from −17 to −24, and see whether the ledge in one.map is still a challenge.
  • Make the sneakers slower: change the 8s in sequences 5 and 6 to 6, and see how wide a canyon they can cross.
  • Move the stars to the far end of level 1, so the hero has to find them before the ledge makes sense.
  • Give a power to another key: copy a sequence, give it a key and a counter of 0, and add a block that adds to it.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie has two short levels to cross. The exit sits on a ledge too high to reach, until a star gives them high jumps. A canyon is too wide to jump, until a pair of sneakers lets them run and leap twice as far. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change how much a star gives.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
A star gives four high jumps; sneakers give fifty fast strides
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Two short levels about powers. The exit is up on a ledge too high to jump, until a star gives you high jumps. A canyon is too wide to cross, until a pair of sneakers lets you run and leap twice as far. A power is a block that adds to a counter, so it lasts for jumps or strides, not seconds. Signs say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change how much a star gives.

57.long: Jump. With a star it is a high jump (4 per star). Steer with Left and Right in the air.

75.long: Walk left. With the sneakers on, twice as fast.

77.long: Walk right. With the sneakers on, twice as fast.

counters.5: Sneaker strides to the right, 50 per sneaker.
counters.6: Sneaker strides to the left, 50 per sneaker.
counters.20: Keys: not used here, but a copy can add them.
